messages:
dana-sales: heads-up — BigFirm wants final commit proposal. They want guaranteed throughput numbers + a burst plan for demo week.
rick-se: paste the traffic profile here if you have it.
dana-sales: attached: baseline 180 RPS gen steady, evening events cause 2.5k RPS bursts lasting ~6-10 minutes, average 280 tokens, chat + rerank + 10% embeddings. 99th latency target 350ms for control-plane ops.
zoe-ml: is chat single long-context model or do they route to a family of models? multi-model routing changes cache effectiveness.
dana-sales: multi-model: 60% long-context chat (~3k ctx), 25% medium chat, 15% embeddings/rerank. Fanout spikes from webhook -> ~4-6x concurrent requests quickly.
rick-se: rough quickcalc: with quantized LLM and aggressive batching + KV cache hit ~35%, an A100-eq node handles ~200 steady mixed RPS. For a 2.5k burst we'd need ~14 warm nodes just for raw throughput. Add headroom for streaming and cold starts.
nate-fin: for the proposal we need two commit tiers: conservative (p99 guardrails) and economical (p95). give baseline GPU counts for both.
rick-se: propose:
- Economical (p95): baseline 12 reserved, burst to 40 via burst pool (spot + on-demand). Autoscale target util 0.65.
- Conservative (p99): baseline 20 reserved, burst to 48, cross-AZ spread.
zoe-ml: notes: long-context chat spikes consume memory and slow batching. preheat behavior is critical. Recommend prewarm window 8-12 minutes for model weights + KV population in production traffic sims.
kelly-ps: customer requires single-tenant GPU pools and KMS controls. that'll be in the security matrix; ok for sizing but impacts ops runbook.
infra-bot: Reserve intent logged: reserve-78910 (proposed 12->40). pending approval.
rick-se: sample autoscale JSON to include in PO (paste as snippet):

"""
{
  \"policy\": \"utilization_target\",
  \"target_util\": \"0.65\",
  \"scale_up\": { \"step_nodes\": \"6\", \"cooldown_s\": \"180\" },
  \"scale_down\": { \"step_nodes\": \"3\", \"cooldown_s\": \"300\" },
  \"preheat\": { \"enabled\": \"true\", \"window_s\": \"600\", \"min_warm\": \"12\" },
  \"burst_pool\": { \"enabled\": \"true\", \"max_nodes\": \"40\", \"spot_fallback\": \"true\" }
}
"""

rick-se: explanation: bigger scale_up step to avoid repeated micro-scales during the 6-10m spikes and to get capacity online quickly. preheat min_warm set to baseline for deterministic demos.
kelly-ps: ops ask: during preheat, do we reuse nodes across customers? security requires per-tenant pools for Private/Dedicated. confirm in PO that preheating uses tenant-isolated nodes only.
zoe-ml: also propose a short perf smoke test runbook: 5m ramp to 2.5k RPS, hold 8m, observe p95/p99 tail latencies and kv-hit ratio. capture token distribution.
nate-fin: preliminary pricing calc: commit discounts change materially between 12->20 baseline. I'll model both options and attach spreadsheet. need expected monthly on-demand cost for A100-eq (quantized) and expected discount %.
dana-sales: customer also asked about AZ resilience — prefer active/active across 3 AZs if possible.
rick-se: active/active 3 AZs is possible but increases baseline (more replicas) and reduces packing efficiency. for p99 we'd recommend 20 distributed as ~7/7/6 and allow burst to fill across AZs.
infra-bot: preheat audit event required: audit-evt-3345 created.
kelly-ps: security will require encrypted preheat logs and an audit trail for any model preload keys. I'll add that to the security appendix.
rick-se: operational risk: spot pool can be reclaimed mid-burst. recommend a mixture: burst pool uses spot + short-duration on-demand credit reserve (we can hold 10% of burst as on-demand to ensure continuity).
nate-fin: question for sales: does customer accept pay-as-you-go for burst nodes or want committed burst credits? committed burst credits reduce margin but give predictability.
dana-sales: they prefer a monthly committed baseline and burst credits they can pre-purchase, but open to pay-as-you-go if price competitive.
zoe-ml: final perf recommendation: run a scaled perf test with realistic routing mix and simulate webhook fanout. collect cold/warm start latencies and KV cache warmup curves.
rick-se: I'll draft the two PO options and include autoscale JSON, preheat guarantees, AZ layout, and the smoke test runbook.
kelly-ps: I'll add the security verbiage on tenant isolation + KMS + encrypted audit logs.
nate-fin: I'll upload price models in 2 hours: https://redwood.drive/BigFirm/pricing-drafts
dana-sales: scheduling follow-up: sign-off call tomorrow 11am PT. tagging BigFirm contact to confirm demo window.
infra-bot: Reserve intent updated: reserve-78910 -> approved-pending-billing.
rick-se: anything else? If not, I'll put the two commit options in the PO and flag the perf test as pre-signature acceptance criteria.
dana-sales: that's it from me. thanks team :rocket:
